name: Purdue NLP Group
researchArea: Natural language processing, language grounding, political discourse analysis, LLMs
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] NLP group in CS, 7 people. Funding (simulated): an NSF award bought us 2 H100 GPU-years on Gautschi (17,520 GPU-hours, resets July 1) and our department share is 4x A100-80GB on Gilbreth. The Gautschi bank is nearly gone (~3,100 hours left), so push anything that fits on 80GB A100s to Gilbreth first. IMMEDIATE: author-response experiments are due Friday Nov 20, 5 pm ET (LoRA fine-tunes of Llama-3-8B on ~40 GB of a licensed political-discourse corpus). Next: ACL 2027 via ARR, mid-February. Data: the corpus is licensed under a data-use agreement - it must stay on Purdue storage (no AWS). Rules: final runs never on preemptible or standby; sweeps can use standby. Any single run over 500 GPU-hours needs PI approval. We use bf16 + FlashAttention-2, so A100/H100 only - no A30s.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Deadline-crunch lab (demo A): Gautschi bank down to ~3k H100-hours. Sources: lab site https://purduenlp.github.io/; faculty page https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/faculty/dgoldwas.html.

name: IDEAS Lab (Intelligent Design for Exploration and Augmented Systems)
researchArea: Computer vision and graphics, generative 3D scenes and world models, human motion prediction
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] Vision/graphics lab, 6 people. Most compute is an NSF ACCESS Discover award (1.5M credits exchanged for Anvil CPU/GPU/AI, ends Mar 31 2027) - ~82% already used, mostly H100s on Anvil ai. Small startup share on Gilbreth (2x A100-40GB). Deadlines: CVPR 2027 supplementary material + code ~Nov 24, ICCV 2027 early March. Our generative 3D scene model trains on 4-8 GPUs for ~2 days; Anvil caps us at 12 GPUs per user and 32 per allocation, and 48 h walltime, so we chain jobs with checkpoints. Warn the PI before we drop under 150k credits so we can file a supplement. Kill Jupyter sessions that hold GPUs overnight.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Runs mostly on (simulated) NSF ACCESS credits on Anvil gpu/ai. Sources: lab site https://ideas.cs.purdue.edu/; faculty page https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/faculty/bera89.html.

name: Slipchenko Group (Theoretical Chemistry)
researchArea: Condensed-phase quantum chemistry, QM/MM with the effective fragment potential (EFP), excited states in photosynthetic proteins
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] Theoretical chemistry group, 8 members. We own 256 cores (2 half-node shares) on Negishi and 1 H100 GPU-year on Gautschi, plus an ACCESS Explore award on Anvil for throughput. Typical jobs: QM/MM and EFP excited-state calculations (Q-Chem, GAMESS) - CPU heavy, 1-14 days, MPI across 2-8 nodes - and GPU molecular dynamics (OpenMM) to sample snapshots of light-harvesting proteins. Big one: a 6-day MD sampling run for a JCTC revision (illustrative date Dec 18). Gautschi ai normal QOS dropped to 4 days on Nov 2, so long GPU runs must go preemptible with checkpoints every 30 min (--signal=B:USR1@600 --requeue). Exploratory sweeps always use standby. SU efficiency matters more than speed - cheapest plan unless a deadline is close.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Long CPU quantum-chemistry jobs + GPU MD sampling; demo C (preemption-safe 6-day run). Sources: lab site https://slipchenko-group.github.io/; faculty page https://www.chem.purdue.edu/people/profile/lslipche.

name: Kihara Lab
researchArea: Protein structure modeling from cryo-EM maps, protein-protein docking, structure and function prediction
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures and the data restriction are illustrative] Structural bioinformatics lab, 5 people. Our Gilbreth purchase is 4x A100-80GB + 2x A30. Workloads: deep-learning cryo-EM map modeling (DeepMainmast, CryoREAD), AlphaFold2-based complex modeling and docking - 1-2 GPUs, 2-10 h, GPU-memory heavy for large complexes. Demo scenario: one collaborator's unpublished cryo-EM maps are covered by a restrictive data agreement - they may only be processed on Purdue-owned Gilbreth nodes under our account, never on Anvil/ACCESS or any cloud. Deliverable to that collaborator Dec 1. Next venue: ISMB 2027 (late January).
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Restricted collaborator data in the demo scenario: Gilbreth only (no ACCESS, no cloud). Sources: lab site https://kiharalab.org/; faculty page https://www.bio.purdue.edu/People/profile/dkihara.html.

name: CoRAL Lab (Cognitive Robot Autonomy and Learning)
researchArea: Physics-informed robot learning, neural motion planning, dexterous and deformable manipulation
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] Robot learning lab, 7 people. Compute: 1 H100 GPU-year on Gautschi (mostly run preemptible at 0.25x so it stretches) plus 2x A30 on Gilbreth; L40S smallgpu for simulation rendering. RL and differentiable-simulation runs are simulator-bound: GPU util is often 20-40% - recommend cheaper GPUs when util is low. Checkpoint every 20 min on preemptible. Quiet hours: weekdays 9am-5pm our 2 A30s are reserved for interactive debugging with the real robots, so batch training should go elsewhere then. Deadlines: thesis committee demo Dec 10, RSS 2027 late January. Nobody launches >8 GPUs without asking the PI.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Many short simulation jobs; GPU util often low (simulator-bound) in the demo history. Sources: lab site https://purdue-corallab.github.io; faculty page https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/faculty/qureshi7.

name: Climate Dynamics Prediction Laboratory
researchArea: Paleoclimate modeling, regional climate modeling, extreme weather and heat stress
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] Climate modeling group in EAPS, 12 people. Workhorses are CESM paleoclimate simulations and WRF regional downscaling (MPI, 4-56 nodes, 6-12 h per ensemble member) on Anvil under an ACCESS Accelerate award (3M credits, ~64% used, ends Mar 31 2027). Post-processing ran on Bell for years; Bell was retired Oct 31 and we are moving those scripts to Gautschi cpu (2 x 48-core units). Anvil scratch purges after 30 days with no warning - copy model output to Depot. Deadlines: AGU Fall Meeting poster in December (regional heat-stress ensemble must finish by Dec 2), EGU 2027 abstracts mid-January. Small ML emulator project on Anvil A100s. Wide queue only allows 12 h, so long members must checkpoint/restart.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Migrating post-processing off Bell (retired 2026-10-31) to Gautschi. Sources: lab site https://web.ics.purdue.edu/~huberm/Climate_Dynamics_Prediction_Laboratory/CDPL.html; faculty page https://eaps.purdue.edu/people/faculty-pages/huber.html.

name: ABE Plant Sensor Lab
researchArea: Hyperspectral plant phenotyping, handheld leaf sensors, greenhouse and field phenotyping, digital agriculture
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] Plant sensing lab, 4 people. We don't own much: 1x A10 on Gilbreth from the department and $25,000 of AWS cloud research credits (expire Jan 14 2027) used for p4d bursts when Gilbreth is busy - about $1,200 left. Spot instances are fine for training (we checkpoint every epoch); on-demand only for a sponsor demo. Hyperspectral plant imagery is not sensitive. A sponsor milestone report on Nov 27 needs the hyperspectral leaf segmentation model retrained on the 2026 season (~1.2 TB of images). Stop anything that would overspend the credits - at 95% hold new AWS jobs and tell the PI. ASABE 2027 abstracts are due in January.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Small (simulated) budget; cloud credits nearly exhausted - budget-burn demo. Sources: lab site https://engineering.purdue.edu/ABEPlantSensorLab; faculty page https://engineering.purdue.edu/~jinjian/Index.htm.

name: Mannodi Group (Computational Materials Design)
researchArea: High-throughput DFT + machine learning for semiconductors, point defects, halide perovskites, ML interatomic potentials
contextDump: [Simulated lab context for the EasyCompute demo - figures are illustrative] Computational materials group, 6 people. We bought the 5 GPU-year package on Gautschi ai (43,800 H100-hours this fiscal year, normal QOS cap max(2, 2x5) = 10 GPUs concurrently) and are at ~88% used in November - burn is ahead of plan. Main run: pretraining a 1.3B-parameter graph-network interatomic potential on high-throughput DFT data on 8x H100 for a paper submission on Jan 28. Our 6-day jobs were legal before Nov 2; now normal QOS is 4 days, so they must be split or go preemptible. The dataloader is a known bottleneck (LMDB on scratch) - if GPUs sit idle, scale the job down rather than letting it burn. Notify the PI when projected burn would exhaust the bank before the deadline.
notes: Illustrative demo data - allocations, usage and deadlines are simulated; lab and PI names from public Purdue pages. Biggest Gautschi H100 user in the demo; over fair share; demos B (idle GPUs + burn) and D (policy change). Sources: faculty page https://engineering.purdue.edu/Engr/People/NewFaculty/New_Faculty_2021/Kanakkithodi.html.
